issue_context.title: `tidb_enable_noop_variables` cannot be set to `WARN`
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

This is introduced by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/35496.

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

```sql
mysql> set global tidb_enable_noop_variables='warn';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> show variables like 'tidb_enable_noop_variables';
+----------------------------+-------+
| Variable_name              | Value |
+----------------------------+-------+
| tidb_enable_noop_variables | OFF   |
+----------------------------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from information_schema.variables_info where variable_name='tidb_enable_noop_variables';
+----------------------------+-----------------+---------------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------------+---------+
| VARIABLE_NAME              | VARIABLES_SCOPE | DEFAULT_VALUE | CURRENT_VALUE | MIN_VALUE | MAX_VALUE | POSSIBLE_VALUES | IS_NOOP |
+----------------------------+-----------------+---------------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------------+---------+
| tidb_enable_noop_variables | GLOBAL          | ON            | OFF           |      NULL |      NULL | OFF,ON,WARN     | NO      |
+----------------------------+-----------------+---------------+---------------+-----------+-----------+-----------------+---------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

`set global tidb_enable_noop_variables='warn';` should report a warning or error.
`POSSIBLE_VALUES` should not include `warn`.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

`possible_values` includes `warn`, but it cannot be set to `warn`.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

master.

review_comments: Also please include a test for setting it to 'warn', which is the reported issue.

Done. But I think it is not very necessary. When set `SET GLOBAL tidb_enable_noop_variables = 2` it means only 0 (OFF) and 1 (ON) are valid values, so it can grantee that all other values are rejected.
Is it better to use `TypeBool` for `TiDBEnableNoopVariables` directly?

Yes, I think `TypeBool` is better. But it is a little different for `TypeBool` and `TypeEnum` 

TypeEnum:
```
mysql> select @@global.tidb_enable_noop_variables;
+-------------------------------------+
| @@global.tidb_enable_noop_variables |
+-------------------------------------+
| ON                                  |
+-------------------------------------+
```

TypeBool:
```
mysql> select @@global.tidb_enable_noop_variables;
+-------------------------------------+
| @@global.tidb_enable_noop_variables |
+-------------------------------------+
| 1                                   |
+-------------------------------------+
```

This variable has been published in 6.2. I'm not sure whether this compatibility break can make a big effect...
I don't think it will 'break' the user.
I still kept it as `TypeEnum` to keep it the same type with `tidb_enable_noop_functions` . In the future if we want to add new value such as `error` , we need not to modify it again.
